title: Investigate and remediate quantized-kernel <-> attention-tile scheduler interlock causing sporadic p99+ latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a capacity surge on 2026-02-15 we observed intermittent p99+ tail latency spikes for a subset of hosted customers using mixed-quant model variants. Root cause appears to be an interaction between the scheduler's probe/autoscale window, deterministic kernel scoring for quantized paths, and attention tiling heuristics that produce cache fragmentation under load. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and medium/long-term fixes to eliminate the interlock and prevent recurrence.

Scope: affects hosted API and Dedicated pools running quantized model variants with long context lengths (>2k), primarily when autoscale events and aggressive scheduler probing occur simultaneously. Not observed on fully-fp16 paths.

Detection: triggered by internal alert runtime.latency.p99_over_threshold and customer escalations (INC-20260215-07). Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/runtime-p99, incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/INC/Quant-Attn-Interlock-2026-02-15.

Desired outcome: remove pathological tail latency events by introducing immediate circuit-breakers, stabilizing kernel ranking, and adding cache-aware scheduling heuristics. Ultimately converge on an execution path scorer resilient to quantization / attention tiling artifacts.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage completed. Reproduced a narrow synthetic reproduction on dedicated dev cluster using seq_len=4096 + mixed-int8 path. Observed batch eviction and KV cache churn correlated with p99 spikes.

2026-02-19 - Miguel Gomez: Binary search narrowed to three interacting factors: (1) quantized kernel preferring smaller GEMM tiling, (2) attention autotile splitting that creates extra KV cache entries, (3) scheduler probe windows that reschedule requests mid-prefix causing cache invalidation. Preparing repro harness and perf trace collection (perf and nvprof).

2026-02-20 - QA (Rachel Chen): Synthetic repro attached: github.com/redwood-inference/repros/quant-attn-interlock, test script and perf traces uploaded. Repro reliably shows p99 jump when concurrent probe window is enabled.

2026-02-22 - Miguel Gomez: Hotfix proposal: (A) add scheduler probe backoff when a kernel-scoring threshold flip occurs; (B) detect attention-split churn and delay scheduling for in-flight KV cache warmups for 300ms. Opened PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127.
2026-02-24 - PM (Samir Rao): Prioritized as P0 due to customer impact. Approve emergency deploy for hotfix with canary to 5% traffic. Ensure rollback path documented.
2026-02-25 - Release (Anita Li): Canary rollout of PR 4127 to 5% passed 24h smoke. Metrics show p99 reduced from 820ms -> 190ms for affected traces. Proceed to 50% canary.
2026-02-26 - Incident commander (Aisha Patel): Post-deploy validation shows no further customer escalations. Next steps: schedule medium-term work to avoid relying on heuristics (see action items).

2026-03-01 - Eng review (Thomas Nguyen): Code review feedback on PR 4127: ensure scheduler backoff config is non-critical path and guard with feature flag runtime.features.probe_backoff. Added unit tests for the backoff timer. PR updated.
2026-03-02 - Security (Mika Othman): Verified no new secrets or KMS changes. Feature flag gating approved.
2026-03-05 - Miguel Gomez: This ticket broken into follow-up subtasks for medium and long term; keeping open until medium-term refactor lands in runtime-2.5.0.
action_items: Short-term (hotfix, deployed 2026-02-25): enable scheduler probe backoff when kernel-score delta > 0.35 (owner: Miguel Gomez).
Short-term: introduce KV-warmup delay for attention-split flows (300ms) to allow cache stabilization during autoscale (owner: QA/Runtime team).

Medium-term (runtime-2.5.0): refactor kernel ranking to include cache-warmth and attention-tiling penalty features; replace brittle thresholds with smoothed scores (owner: Thomas Nguyen, estimate 13d).
Medium-term: add targeted perf benchmarks to CI that simulate autoscale probe windows + mixed-quant stack (owner: Perf team, add to nightly).

Long-term: train a small lightweight ML-based path scorer that predicts end-to-end latency and selects kernel + attention config per-request; integrate with canary framework (owner: Research/Applied ML, estimate 3 sprints).

Operational: add an alert that correlates 'kernel_score_flip' events with p99 spikes and fires a runbook (owner: SRE, runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RUN/Kernel-Flip-Runbook).
Customer comms: prepare a post-incident summary for affected customers and update status page entry (owner: Samir Rao).
